extracted.intended_audience: prospective depositors of biological materials for patent purposes (patent applicants, microbiologists, culture collection depositors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and making deposits of microorganisms, plasmids, cell lines and related biological material under the Budapest Treaty, including technical form/quantity, viability testing, administrative procedures, sample furnishing, and applicable fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of Microorganisms that May Be Deposited
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists the types of biological material each collection will accept and any explicit exclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples across collections: archaea, bacteria, fungi (including yeasts and molds), plasmids, bacteriophages and plant viruses; plant cell cultures, human and animal cell cultures; human and animal cell lines and hybridomas (subject to storage/containment limits). Common exclusions or restrictions include obligate human pathogenic species (e.g., Corynebacterium diphtheriae, Mycobacterium leprae, Yersinia pestis), certain pathogenic fungi (Blastomyces, Coccidioides, Histoplasma, etc.), viruses/phages/rickettsiae/algae/protozoa/cell lines/hybridomas in some collections, mixed cultures (not accepted unless sent separately), and organisms above allowed hazard/containment categories. Many collections reserve the right to refuse material that is an unacceptable hazard or cannot be processed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to refuse deposits / hazard and technical suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Collection may refuse a deposit if it represents an unacceptable hazard or cannot be processed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections explicitly reserve the right to refuse material for safety or technical reasons. Some will accept pathogenic material only if cleared by appropriate national authorities. Genetically manipulated organisms are accepted only if processable in specified biosafety levels (e.g., BSL-1/BSL-2 or S1/S2) or if they conform to local hazard group classifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and Quantity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific physical form and minimum quantities that depositors must supply for different kinds of material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements vary by collection and organism type: NCAIM requires 25 replicates for lyophilized preparations or 3 for active cultures; MCC asks for two active cultures on slants for bacteria/fungi and 5x20 µg of plasmid DNA plus hosts (2 slants each); MTCC requires 10 freeze-dried ampoules and 2 active cultures for bacteria/fungi, bacteriophages 5 x 2 ml with minimum titre 1 x 10^9 pfu/ml plus host (2 slants), plasmids 5 x 20 µg plus host (2 slants); ABC (cell lines/hybridomas) requires at least 12 frozen ampoules with not less than 2 x 10^6 cells per ampoule; IZSLER needs twelve vials at concentration no less than 10^5 viable units/vial; DBVPG specifies test tubes in liquid/gel or freeze-dried ampoules and frozen cultures shipped with sufficient dry ice. If deposit packaging/shipping is inadequate, cultures may be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum purity / contamination requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposited material must be pure and free from contamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections require samples to be pure (uncontaminated). DBVPG states that in presence of contamination by bacteria, molds, other yeasts and acarina, the dispatched culture is immediately sterilized. IZSLER requires material tested and free from contamination by foreign microorganisms by the depositor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time required for viability testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Expected time ranges for the collection to test viability of deposited material, acknowledging variability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Times vary by organism and collection: NCAIM average 7 days (may be as long as 14); MCC bacteria/yeast/plasmids 4 days to 3 weeks, actinomycetes/fungi 7 days to 4 weeks; MTCC bacteria/yeast/bacteriophages/plasmids 4 days to 3 weeks, fungi 7 days to 4 weeks; ABC (cell lines/hybridomas) 10–14 days (may be longer); DBVPG average 20 days; IZSLER bacteria average 14 days (up to 3 weeks), human/animal viruses average 20 days. Depositors should realize slow-growing organisms require longer testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositor checks and renewal of stocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for the collection preparing batches, depositor verification, and renewal of diminishing stocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many collections (NCAIM, MCC, MTCC, DBVPG) will prepare their own batches by subculturing active cultures and will send samples of new batches for the depositor to check authenticity. Collections that receive lyophilized preparations may not prepare their own batches. Diminishing stocks are renewed by requesting the depositor to make a new deposit. Collections commonly store a portion of the original material supplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Official languages accepted by each collection for communications and forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: NCAIM official language Hungarian but accepts English, French, German and Russian; MCC and MTCC use English and accept Hindi (English prevails in disputes); ABC official language Italian but accepts English and French. Collections specify which languages forms and notifications will be in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract / depositor agreement and surrender of withdrawal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositor must complete and sign required deposit forms and by doing so accept terms, including surrendering right to withdraw deposit during required storage period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections generally do not enter into separate written contracts; however, by signing the deposit form the depositor surrenders the right to withdraw the deposit during required storage. Forms often include declarations on pathogenicity, agreement to deposit only in required form/quantity, agreement to comply with the Budapest Treaty and collection-specific requirements, and acceptance to pay all required fees and shipping costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Import and quarantine requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement for depositors to ensure compliance with import/quarantine regulations for incoming cultures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some collections note that certain microorganisms may be subject to import or quarantine regulations and depositors from outside the country should communicate with the collection before dispatching or obtain necessary clearances/import permits. MTCC, MCC, and others explicitly warn about import clearance and quarantine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory BP and international forms for deposit and notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of the Budapest Treaty ‘international forms’ (BP forms) for receipts, viability statements, amendments, attestations, requests and notifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard forms: BP/1 for original deposit (accession), BP/2 for new deposit, BP/4 and BP/5 for receipts, BP/9 for viability statement, BP/7 for amendment of scientific description/taxonomic designation, BP/8 for attestation of receipt of amendments, BP/12 for proof of entitlement, BP/13 for request, BP/14 to notify depositor when sample furnished. Collections issue mandatory international forms for official notifications and may use their own letters for other notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converting a previous (non‑Budapest) deposit to a Budapest Treaty deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and conditions to convert earlier deposits to Budapest Treaty deposits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original depositors may convert deposits made outside Treaty provisions to Budapest Treaty deposits. Conversion is subject to the same storage fees normally levied for Budapest Treaty deposits and the same administrative requirements. If a previous deposit is listed in a public catalogue without distribution restrictions, collections may require the depositor to waive notification rights or otherwise require a fresh deposit if conditions are unacceptable to the depositor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making a new deposit (procedural requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms and documents required when making a subsequent/new deposit, and issuance of receipts/viability statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor must complete BP/2 when making a new deposit and supply the relevant documents required by Rule 6.2. Receipts and viability statements for new deposits are issued on BP/5 and BP/9 respectively. Collections may require shipping notices (e.g., notify 48 hours before shipping, give flight number/carrier for air shipments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for samples / proof of entitlement / requester qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements a requesting party must meet to validly request and receive furnished samples from a collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesting parties must demonstrate entitlement (use BP/12 and/or BP/13) and typically must show they are trained in microbiology and have access to a properly equipped laboratory or provide evidence of proper facility/permissions for hazardous organisms. For overseas requests, requester is assumed to have met their country's import requirements and may need to provide an import permit if required. Collections may furnish samples prepared by the collection from the deposited sample(s) or from depositor-supplied preparations depending on deposit form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to depositor when samples furnished
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections notify the depositor when samples of their deposit have been furnished to third parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification is issued on BP/14 form. Some collections will send copies of receipt and viability statement to the depositor and, on request, to the depositor's patent agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cataloguing and public listing of Budapest Treaty deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Budapest Treaty deposits are listed in the collection's published catalogue or online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many collections explicitly state they do not publish Budapest Treaty deposits in their printed or electronic catalogues or display them on the internet (e.g., NCAIM, MCC, MTCC, DBVPG). Others may maintain internal records but not public listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of Fees and fee categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee types that apply to deposits and related administrative acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common fee items include: storage (Rule 12.1(a)(i)), conversion of a deposit, extension/prolongation of duration of storage (per year) under Rule 9, issuance of a viability statement (on the basis of a test or on the basis of the last viability test), furnishing of a sample, communication of information under Rule 7.6, attestation referred to in Rule 8.2, and issuance of attestations/communications/requests to competent authorities. Collections list amounts in local currency (examples in the text: HUF 150,000 storage; various EUR and INR amounts for other centers). VAT and processing fees may apply for domestic/EU customers and on invoices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage and preservation methods and required conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted long-term preservation/storage methods and temperature requirements for deposited material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials are generally preserved by freeze-drying (lyophilized), frozen storage (including liquid nitrogen), or other long-term preservation methods. IZSLER stores at -20°C and -80°C according to preservation method; DBVPG requires frozen cultures shipped with sufficient dry ice guaranteeing 48 hours autonomy. ABC requires cell line ampoules sent with enough dry ice to remain frozen during transport.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shipping and packaging requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for packaging and transport to ensure material arrives intact and acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections require sufficient dry ice or packaging to maintain frozen state for transport (e.g., ABC: sufficient dry ice; DBVPG: containers of expanded polystyrene with enough dry ice for 48 hours). If the package is found inadequate, the culture may not be accepted. Depositors often must inform the collection before shipping (e.g., 48 hours notice, flight number, airway bill).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply of information to a patent agent
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the collection will send receipts/viability statements to a depositor's patent agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most collections will, if requested, send copies of the receipt and viability statement to both the depositor and their patent agent; collections do not routinely ask for the patent agent's details but will comply upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unofficial notifications and interim communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections' practice on providing unofficial/early information (e.g., date of deposit, accession number, viability results) before issuing official forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requested, many collections will telephone or e-mail the date of deposit and accession number after receipt but before the official receipt is issued, or communicate viability test results before issuance of the official viability statement, typically only after a positive viability test is obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: No mixed cultures policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Mixed microbiological cultures typically are not accepted unless components are sent separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IZSLER and other collections state that no mixed microbiological cultures will be accepted; if components are to be deposited they must be sent separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance and help for depositors
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of written notes, forms, and advisory help for prospective depositors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some collections (e.g., DSMZ, MCC, MTCC, MTCC/DBVPG/MTCC etc.) provide specific written notes on their websites and are ready to give advice by telephone or e-mail; others do not produce standard guidance notes (e.g., NCAIM stated it does not at present produce standard notes). Deposit forms often contain recommendations for depositors.
